tools.name: syntaxcheck
tools.description:
Analyzes BSL code for syntax errors using bsl-analyzer.

This tool takes a string of BSL code, saves it to a temporary file,
runs bsl-analyzer on it, and returns the analysis report as a string
in TOON format (one document under an "events" key: a "start" event, a
"file" event whose diagnostics are written as one table, and a "done"
summary event).

'file_name' says what the code is: give it 'ObjectModule.bsl' and the
analyzer sees an object module under that name, and every location in the
answer is that name rather than a temporary path of this server's. It is a
name and not a location - a path separator, a parent segment, an absolute
or drive-qualified form, a control character, an empty stem or an extension
bsl-analyzer does not read fails the call with the reason rather than being
quietly replaced, because a name this server repaired is a difference the
caller cannot see. Omit it and the call behaves exactly as it did before
the argument existed.

Beside the analyzer's findings the report carries platform names the
platform does not have, checked against the analyzer's own platform model:
UnknownPlatformMethod (a method of a variable created by Новый <Тип> in the
same method), UnknownPlatformProperty, UnknownSystemEnumValue,
UnknownPlatformType (Новый <Имя>) and, for code sent here as text,
PlatformApiUnavailableOnClient (a server-only type or global function in a
&НаКлиенте method). "provenance": {"platform_names": ...} says whether the
model was ready for the call.

code.description: A string containing the BSL code to be analyzed.

file_name.description: Optional logical module name for the submitted code, e.g. "ObjectModule.bsl". A bare file name ending in .bsl - never a path. Empty analyses the code under a generic name.

outputSchema.description: The analysis, and what shaped it. The same report is returned as text beside this, written as one TOON document.

diagnostics.description: Every diagnostic the response carries, in order.

file.description: The analysed file, as the caller addressed it.

message.description: as the analyzer wrote it, or as a plugin annotated it

severity.description: as the analyzer wrote it, or as a plugin annotated it

start_line.description: counted from the base provenance.line_base declares

end_line.description: counted from the base provenance.line_base declares

start_column.description: counted from the base provenance.line_base declares

end_column.description: counted from the base provenance.line_base declares

total.description: How many diagnostics the analyzer produced, before anything shaped the list.

returned.description: How many are present in this response.

truncated.description: Whether this response is an incomplete rendering of the analysis. Filtering and suppression are described by the flags and by total versus returned, not by this.

filters.description: Which mechanisms shaped the list. Each states that it applied, never which code it removed or which plugin acted.

severity_filter_applied.description: Always false: this product applies no severity filter.

analyzer_version.description: The bsl-analyzer release this container is running, which it keeps up to date with upstream.

bundled_configuration.description: Whether the analyzer ran with the bundled bsl-analyzer.toml.

source_encoding.description: The encoding the source under analysis was read as.

line_base.description: The base every line number here is counted from.

file_metrics_scope.description: What the metrics of the text form's file events describe: whole_file, the analysed file as a whole. They are never narrowed by the lines argument, so a narrowed diagnostics list is not a narrowed file.

index.description: Whether the whole configuration was available to this call, and therefore whether a cross-module reference was checked at all. absent: this server keeps no index, so an unresolved call or field was not looked for. building: it is indexing and had not finished. ready: every check ran, this one included. failed: the index could not be built and the call was answered without one. A clean report means different things under absent and under ready, and this is how to tell them apart.

platform_names.description: Whether this call checked the platform names the code uses - methods of platform types, system enumeration values, types after Новый - against the analyzer's platform model. ready: checked. loading: the model was still being read. unavailable: it could not be read, so those names were not checked.

request_rewrite.description: Whether a plugin changed the arguments of this call, and to what. The same information the text form carries as its synthetic plugin_request event.

diagnostic_asides.description: Fields carried beside the diagnostics rather than inside them, because a diagnostic's row admits only primitive values. `tags` is what the analyzer puts here; a plugin's annotation that is not a primitive arrives here too. Each entry names the diagnostic it belongs to by its index in the list above, and one value per entry, so a field the analyzer wrote as a list of two arrives as two entries. Empty when there was nothing to carry.

field.description: the field this value was written as

tools.name: syntaxcheck_file
tools.description:
Analyzes a BSL file from the mounted files directory for syntax errors.

This is a project-file read mode, and that is its contract, and where
a directory is mounted it is the way to check code that lives in it:
the file is analysed under its own name and in its own place, and
`syntaxcheck` is for code that has no file yet.

What this tool can say depends on whether the container keeps an index.
Without one - the default - three diagnostics are switched off, because
a call analysing one module cannot resolve a call, a field or a query's
metadata against the rest of the configuration and would report every
cross-module reference as unresolved. Started with FULLINDEX=true the
container indexes the mounted directory and takes those three from that
index once it is ready, which costs seconds per call rather than
milliseconds. Either way the answer says which it was, in
"provenance": {"index": ...} - absent, building, ready or failed - so a
clean report can be read for what it is.

Platform names are checked whatever the index state, as in
`syntaxcheck`: UnknownPlatformMethod, UnknownPlatformProperty,
UnknownSystemEnumValue and UnknownPlatformType, with
"provenance": {"platform_names": ...} saying whether the analyzer's
platform model was ready. Availability on the client is the analyzer's
own UnavailableInEnvironment here, because the file's path tells it
what kind of module it is.

The directory mounted at FILES_DIR is the project root; 'file_path' is
scoped to it; the boundary is enforced on the resolved target, with
symbolic links followed, so a link out of the project is refused rather
than read. The caller's own file is what bsl-analyzer is given - not a
copy under a generic name - and if 'lines' is provided, only
diagnostics that affect the specified lines are returned.

What comes back is expressed in the caller's terms, not the server's.
The "file" event names the analysed file relative to the project root,
in POSIX form, so the answer can be acted on and used again unchanged;
no path of this server's own appears in any field of any event, or in
the payload of a refusal. Every range is 1-based - the same base the
'lines' argument is written in - and the report declares it by carrying
"line_base": 1 on its "start" event, so a call narrowed to "10-20"
reads a "start_line" back between 10 and 20.

file_path.description: Path to the BSL file, relative to the mounted files directory.

lines.description: Optional 1-based lines to check, e.g. "5, 10-20, 35". Empty string checks the whole file.

tools.name: plugin_state
tools.description:
Reports the state of the plugin subsystem.

Lists every plugin file that was read, the hooks and tables it declares,
the classification of each hook, whether each is enabled or disabled, the
error that disabled it, its failure count and the time accumulated in it,
plus the order the files run in and the current plugin epoch.

Returns:
    A JSON object describing the plugin subsystem.

tools.name: plugin_reload
tools.description:
Re-reads the plugin directory without restarting the server.

Every plugin file is read again, the hooks in force are replaced in one
step and a new plugin epoch begins. If any file no longer loads, nothing
is replaced: the previously loaded set stays in force and the response
names the file that failed and why.

Returns:
    A JSON object describing what is in force after the reload.
